# Getting started

Source: https://harnex.zyt.app/docs/start

You've installed harnex. Here's how to actually use it.

harnex hands work to Pi workers (GPT models by default) and gives you, or the
agent you are working with, the result back as plain text. Each worker runs in
a visible tmux window you can switch to at any time.

## Check the setup

```bash
harnex doctor          # Pi 0.80.4+ on PATH, tmux, retention; MCP integrations
harnex mcp install     # optional: native tools for Claude Code and Pi
```

## Your first lanes

Ask another model a question. The worker reads the repository, answers and
stops:

```bash
harnex ask "Which module parses the dispatch rows, and is it tested?"
```

Hand a worker a task in its own git worktree, review it, and land it:

```bash
harnex delegate --worktree word-count \
  "Add TextKit.word_count(text) with a test; run bin/test."
git diff HEAD...harnex/word-count
harnex land word-count
```

The worker's reply comes back with a footer that says what happened and what
to do next:

```text
── word-count: done in 49s · gpt-5.1 · $0.03 · 1 commit, 2 files (+12 -0)
   worktree .harnex/worktrees/word-count (branch harnex/word-count)
   next: review `git diff HEAD...harnex/word-count`, then `harnex land word-count` ...
```

Follow up with the same worker; it keeps its context:

```bash
harnex reply word-count "Also add TextKit.char_count(text)."
```

Run several at once, then collect them:

```bash
harnex delegate --no-wait --worktree a "Task A"
harnex delegate --no-wait --worktree b "Task B"
harnex result
harnex land
```

Commands wait up to 9 minutes; if a worker is still going they exit 124 and
`harnex result NAME` keeps waiting. `harnex lanes` shows what each worker is
doing right now. The full guide is [docs/lanes.md](docs/lanes.md); for
driving harnex from Claude Code or Pi, see [docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md)
and [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md).

## Sessions: the layer underneath

Lanes are built on ordinary harnex sessions. The rest of this guide covers
that layer, which you need for custom orchestration, long-lived interactive
workers, and wrapping other terminal agents.

### Recommended mental model

Treat harnex as a local supervisor harness, not as a conversation
bus between agents.

- Start a fresh worker for each step, usually with `--tmux`
- Give one clear startup task with `--context` (or `--context-file`); add `--auto-stop` for one-shot work
- Monitor existing visible work with `harnex watch --until done`
- Use `--wait-for-idle` only as a follow-up-send fence, then verify the artifact
- Ask the worker to write its output to a file when the next step needs it
- Stop completed interactive workers promptly

For multi-step flows, chain fresh workers with file handoffs:
Pi writes a plan, a fresh Pi implements it, Claude (or a fresh Pi
lane) reviews it, another fresh Pi fixes it.

### Your first session

Pi is the default worker. Check that the installed Pi is new enough
(0.80.4 or later), then start it through harnex:

```bash
harnex doctor
harnex run pi
```

Harnex runs Pi in its structured RPC mode (`pi --mode rpc`) and
prints the session as a transcript. Harnex runs alongside it —
registering the session, listening for messages, and tracking
whether the agent is busy or idle. Claude Code, OpenCode, or any
other terminal CLI (`harnex run claude`) runs under a PTY instead and
looks exactly as it does when run directly.

Give it a name so other sessions can find it:

```bash
harnex run pi --id pi-i-13
```

Session IDs follow `<cli>-<role>-<tag>`: `pi-p-13` plans issue 13,
`pi-i-13` implements it, `pi-f-13` fixes it, and `cl-r-13` is a
Claude reviewer. See `harnex agents-guide naming`.

### Sending messages

From another terminal:

```bash
harnex send --id pi-i-13 --message "implement the auth module"
```

If the agent is busy, you don't have to wait or retry: a busy Pi
worker takes the message at once as a follow-up and runs it when the
current turn ends, and other agents queue it until they are back at a
prompt. Follow-ups exist, but the default workflow should still be
one task per fresh worker.

For unattended visible dispatch, prefer the native work-level watcher over
external poll loops:

```bash
harnex run pi --id pi-i-13 --tmux pi-i-13 \
  --context "Read and execute /tmp/task-impl-13.md" --auto-stop
harnex watch --id pi-i-13 --until done --max-wait 90m
```

Or launch and wait in one call. `--wait-done` blocks until the first
turn's result and prints it; the worker's reply is
`turn_result.final_message`. On exit 124 the worker keeps going; run
the `resume` command the output names.

```bash
harnex run pi --id pi-i-13 --tmux pi-i-13 \
  --context "Read and execute /tmp/task-impl-13.md" \
  --auto-stop --wait-done --wait-timeout 9m
```

Pi RPC cannot show Pi's project-trust prompt, so harnex starts Pi with
`--no-approve` (project-local Pi resources ignored); pass `-- --approve` to
load them.

`harnex run --watch --preset impl` is a separate foreground launch-and-stall
babysitter; do not combine it with `--tmux` or `--detach`. For full flag
behavior and event-stream consumers, see
[TECHNICAL.md](TECHNICAL.md) and the built-in monitoring section in
[README.md](README.md).

### Seeing what's running

```bash
harnex status
```

Shows all live sessions for the current repo with their ID, CLI
type, age, and state (prompt/busy).

### Running agents in tmux

This is the recommended way to run multiple agents. Each one gets
its own tmux window you can switch to anytime:

```bash
harnex run pi --id pi-i-13 --tmux pi-i-13
harnex run claude --id cl-r-13 --tmux cl-r-13
```

Pass the same value to `--id` and `--tmux` so status, panes, logs,
and the tmux window name all line up.

Switch between them with your normal tmux keys (`Ctrl-b n`,
`Ctrl-b p`, or `Ctrl-b w` to pick from a list). This is the
easiest way to monitor what each agent is doing. Claude's window
shows its normal TUI; Pi's shows harnex's transcript of the RPC
session rather than Pi's own TUI.

For longer-running work, `harnex pane` lets you peek at an
agent's screen without switching windows:

```bash
harnex pane --id pi-i-13 --lines 30
```

Or watch it live from your current terminal:

```bash
harnex pane --id pi-i-13 --follow
```

### Raw parallel sessions in worktrees

`harnex delegate --worktree` creates and cleans up worktrees for you. To
manage them yourself with raw sessions, give each its own git worktree.
`--cwd` starts Pi in the worktree, `--root` keeps the session attributed to
your main checkout, and harnex credits each session with its own commits:

```bash
git worktree add ../wt-13 -b issue-13
git worktree add ../wt-14 -b issue-14
harnex run pi --id pi-i-13 --tmux pi-i-13 --cwd ../wt-13 --root . \
  --context-file /tmp/task-13.md --auto-stop
harnex run pi --id pi-i-14 --tmux pi-i-14 --cwd ../wt-14 --root . \
  --context-file /tmp/task-14.md --auto-stop
```

Watch each with `harnex watch --id`, or, from a Claude Code or Pi
supervisor, wait for every lane you launched in one call:

```bash
harnex watch --owner --until-idle --timeout 90m
```

A Claude Code subagent shares its parent's session ID; it passes the
same `--owner-tag TAG` to `harnex run` and `harnex watch --owner` so
it sees only its own lanes (`harnex agents-guide claude`).

### Sending work and waiting for it to finish

Use `--wait-for-idle` to block until the agent finishes
processing:

```bash
harnex send --id pi-i-13 --message "implement the plan" --wait-for-idle --timeout 600
```

This is better than separate send + wait commands because there's
no gap where you might check too early and think the agent is
done when it hasn't started yet.

With Pi, `--wait-done` goes further: it blocks until the turn the
message started (or joined) settles and prints that turn's result,
with the same exit codes as `harnex wait --until done`:

```bash
harnex send --id pi-i-13 --message "Also cover the empty-input case." --wait-done --timeout 540
```

Treat `--wait-for-idle` as the fence, not the report. After the
send returns, use `harnex pane` or `harnex logs` to inspect what
actually happened.

### Sending large prompts

Shell quoting and terminal input don't love multi-kilobyte inline
messages. For anything longer than a few sentences, write the
task to a file and tell the agent to read it:

```bash
cat > /tmp/task-impl-13.md <<'EOF'
Implement phase 2 from koder/plans/03_output_streaming.md.

Focus on:
- The HTTP endpoint for streaming output
- Integration with the existing ring buffer
- Tests for the new endpoint

Do not modify the CLI commands.
EOF

harnex send --id pi-i-13 --message "Read and execute /tmp/task-impl-13.md"
```

If the task is already written down — a plan file, an issue, a
spec — just point to it:

```bash
harnex send --id pi-i-13 --message "Implement koder/plans/plan_09_atomic_send_wait.md"
```

At launch, `--context-file` sends a file's text itself as the task,
and `--context-section` sends only the part under one heading:

```bash
harnex run pi --id pi-i-13 --tmux pi-i-13 \
  --context-file koder/briefs/13.md --context-section "## Task" --auto-stop
```

This is more reliable, easier to debug (you can read the file to
see exactly what was sent), and avoids quoting headaches.

### Capturing results

For dependable multi-step work, prefer file handoffs over reply
messages.

Examples:

```bash
# Planning
harnex send --id pi-p-13 --message "Read koder/issues/13_atomic_send_wait.md and write a plan to /tmp/plan-13.md. Do not change code." --wait-for-idle --timeout 600

# Review
harnex send --id cl-r-13 --message "Review the current changes against /tmp/plan-13.md and write findings to /tmp/review-13.md. If clean, say so explicitly." --wait-for-idle --timeout 600
```

Why files work better:

- The next worker can read exactly the same artifact you reviewed
- The supervisor can inspect the artifact without scraping terminal text
- If the session dies, the output still exists

Pi results also carry the worker's last reply as `final_message` (in
`run --wait-done`, `send --wait-done`, and `watch --owner` output).
That is enough for a short answer; use a file for anything the next
step must read.

After the worker finishes, inspect the screen:

```bash
harnex pane --id cl-r-13 --lines 60
```

**Return channel for any tmux pane:** Every spawned session gets
`$HARNEX_SPAWNER_PANE` — the tmux pane ID of whoever ran `harnex run`.
The spawned agent can report back via `tmux send-keys`, even if the
invoker isn't a harnex session:

```bash
tmux send-keys -t "$HARNEX_SPAWNER_PANE" "done — results in /tmp/result.md" Enter
```

If you're inside a harnex-managed session, you can also use
`$HARNEX_ID` as the return address with `harnex send`. But file
handoffs remain the preferred primary control flow.

### Stopping agents

```bash
harnex stop --id pi-i-13
```

For Pi, harnex aborts any running turn and ends the `pi --mode rpc`
process. PTY agents get their native exit sequence (e.g. `/exit` for
Claude). Either way the agent shuts down cleanly.

### A reliable supervised workflow

Use fresh instances for each stage. Pi plans, implements, and fixes.
Claude (or a fresh Pi lane) only reviews.

```bash
# 1. Plan with Pi
harnex run pi --id pi-p-13 --tmux pi-p-13
harnex send --id pi-p-13 --message "Read koder/issues/13_atomic_send_wait.md and write a concrete implementation plan to /tmp/plan-13.md. Do not change code." --wait-for-idle --timeout 600
harnex pane --id pi-p-13 --lines 60
harnex stop --id pi-p-13

# 2. Implement with a fresh Pi
harnex run pi --id pi-i-13 --tmux pi-i-13
harnex send --id pi-i-13 --message "Read /tmp/plan-13.md, implement it, run tests, and write a short summary to /tmp/impl-13.md." --wait-for-idle --timeout 1200
harnex pane --id pi-i-13 --lines 80
harnex stop --id pi-i-13

# 3. Review with a fresh Claude
harnex run claude --id cl-r-13 --tmux cl-r-13
harnex send --id cl-r-13 --message "Review the current changes against /tmp/plan-13.md. Write findings to /tmp/review-13.md. If there are no issues, say clean." --wait-for-idle --timeout 900
harnex pane --id cl-r-13 --lines 80
harnex stop --id cl-r-13
```

If the review finds issues, spawn a fresh Pi fixer (`pi-f-13`) and
tell it to read `/tmp/review-13.md`, fix the findings, run tests, and
write an updated summary. Then review again with a fresh Claude
instance, or a fresh Pi lane (`pi-r-13`) that has not seen the
implementation.

Each Pi step can also be one blocking call:
`harnex run pi --id pi-p-13 --tmux pi-p-13 --context "..." --auto-stop --wait-done --wait-timeout 9m`.

## Teaching agents about harnex

The smoothest way is `harnex mcp install`: Claude Code and Pi get the lane
commands as native tools, and Claude Code gets a `gpt` subagent (see
[docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md)). Harnex also ships its agent guidance in the
CLI; no skill install or project-local docs are required:

```bash
harnex agents-guide             # list all agent guide topics
harnex agents-guide dispatch    # Fire and Watch lifecycle
harnex agents-guide monitoring  # completion signals and polling
harnex agents-guide naming      # session IDs and artifact names
harnex agents-guide claude      # Pi workers as tools from Claude Code
```

Tell an agent to run `harnex --help` and then `harnex agents-guide`.
The guides cover dispatch, chain implementation, buddies, monitoring,
naming conventions, and Claude Code using Pi workers as tools.

## Recipes

Tested workflows for common multi-agent patterns. Read them
from the CLI:

```bash
harnex recipes             # list all recipes
harnex recipes show 01     # read one
harnex agents-guide        # deeper agent-facing guidance
```

- **Fire and Watch** (`harnex recipes show 01`) — send work to a
  fresh worker, watch its tmux screen, capture the result, stop it.
- **Chain Implement** (`harnex recipes show 02`) — process a
  batch as repeated fire-and-watch: Pi plan/implement, Claude (or a
  fresh Pi lane) review, Pi fix, then review again if needed.
- **Buddy** (`harnex recipes show 03`) — spawn an accountability
  partner for overnight or long-running work. The buddy polls the
  worker's screen and nudges it if it stalls.

## What's next

For lanes, MCP and coding agents, see [docs/lanes.md](docs/lanes.md),
[docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md) and [docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md); upgrading
from an older release, [docs/upgrading-to-0.29.md](docs/upgrading-to-0.29.md).
For the full command reference, flags, HTTP API, and internals,
see [TECHNICAL.md](TECHNICAL.md). The packaged
[dispatch telemetry](docs/dispatch-telemetry.md) and
[configuration](docs/configuration.md) references cover the canonical v2 stream,
phase allowlists, and log retention.


---

# Lanes

Source: https://harnex.zyt.app/docs/lanes

A **lane** is one Pi worker doing one job: a question, a task, or a task plus
its follow-ups. You start one with `harnex ask` or `harnex delegate`, collect
it with `harnex result`, continue it with `harnex reply`, and finish it with
`harnex land` or `harnex discard`. Every lane has a name, runs in a visible
tmux window named after it, and leaves a small record so any later command can
find it by name from anywhere in the repository (from any worktree of it, a
bare-repo layout included).

Lanes are the agent-facing layer of harnex. Everything here is also available
as native tools through [`harnex mcp`](mcp.md), and the low-level `run`, `send`,
`wait` and `watch` commands remain underneath for custom orchestration.

| Need | Command |
| --- | --- |
| A second opinion, an explanation, a read-only review | `harnex ask "QUESTION"` |
| A task that edits code | `harnex delegate --worktree NAME "TASK"`, review, then `harnex land NAME` |
| A task that only runs or inspects things | `harnex delegate "TASK"` |
| Several tasks in parallel | `harnex delegate --no-wait --worktree NAME "TASK"` per task, then `harnex result` |
| More work for the same worker, with its context | `harnex reply NAME "MESSAGE"` |
| Throw a lane away | `harnex discard NAME` |
| What is open and what each worker is doing | `harnex lanes` |

## Ask

```bash
harnex ask "Which module writes dispatch rows, and is the lane case tested?"
harnex ask --model openai/gpt-5.1 --file /tmp/review.md
```

The worker reads the repository with read-only tools (`read`, `grep`, `find`,
`ls`), answers, and stops. It cannot run commands or change anything; for
that, use `delegate`. stdout is the answer; stderr gets one line naming the
lane, its time and the model. `--write` lets the worker edit and run commands,
and `--fallback-model M` asks once more with another model when the first one
is out of capacity or rate limited.

Every ask is a lane (`pi-ask-xxxx`), so `harnex reply pi-ask-xxxx "..."` asks a
follow-up of the same worker, with everything it read still in context.

## Delegate

```bash
harnex delegate --worktree word-count \
  "Add TextKit.word_count(text): the number of whitespace-separated words, with a test. Run bin/test."
```

The worker edits files, runs commands, and replies with a summary. harnex
prints that reply and then a footer:

```text
Committed as `a6bf91e` on `harnex/word-count`.
- Added `TextKit.word_count(text)` in `lib/textkit.rb`.
- Ran `bin/test`: 3 tests, 6 assertions, all passing.

── word-count: done in 49s · gpt-5.1 · $0.03 · 1 commit, 2 files (+12 -0)
   worktree .harnex/worktrees/word-count (branch harnex/word-count)
   next: review `git diff HEAD...harnex/word-count`, then `harnex land word-count` ...
```

The footer always says what happened and what to do next: state, time, model,
cost, commits and the next commands.

- **`--worktree NAME`** creates `.harnex/worktrees/NAME` on a new branch
  `harnex/NAME` from `HEAD`. The worker is told to commit there. Parallel lanes
  never collide, and your checkout is untouched until you land. If your checkout
  has uncommitted changes, harnex warns that the worktree starts from `HEAD`.
  A repo that keeps its worktrees elsewhere says so in `.harnex/config.json`
  (see [Where things live](#where-things-live)).
- **Without `--worktree`** the worker works in the current directory, or in
  `--cwd DIR`, which is right for tasks that only run or inspect things (tests,
  a benchmark, a long command) and for a worktree you made yourself.
- **Names.** `--name NAME` names the lane. Otherwise a lane working in another
  worktree of the repo is named after it (`--cwd ../night-1024_s3` gives
  `pi-night-1024_s3`), and any other lane after the task's first words
  (`pi-slow-bench`, then `pi-slow-bench-2`). Generated names skip every name
  another lane still holds anywhere (working, uncollected, or a worktree not
  yet landed), and a name you choose is refused while another repo's worker
  is running under it, so `harnex result NAME` and `reply NAME` find a
  working lane from anywhere.
- **`--file PATH`** reads a long brief from a file. Briefs must be
  self-contained: the worker has not seen your conversation. Name the files, the
  expected behavior and how to verify it.
- **`--model provider/model`** and **`--effort low|medium|high`** pick the
  model; the default is Pi's own default model.
- **`--phase NAME`** tags the lane's dispatch rows with a work phase (for
  example `implement`). Without it the phase is `delegate` (`ask` for an ask),
  which a repo's phase allowlist always accepts; a named phase is checked
  against the allowlist (see [configuration](configuration.md)).

### Waiting, and long tasks

Blocking commands (`ask`, `delegate`, `reply`, `result`) wait up to 9 minutes
by default, which fits under the 10-minute tool cap most coding agents have.
`--timeout DUR` changes it (`540`, `9m`, `1h30m`, or `none`).

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | done |
| 1 | the worker failed (the footer says why and what to try) |
| 2 | usage error (nothing was started) |
| 124 | still working — the worker keeps going; run `harnex result NAME` |

```text
── slow-bench: still working (9m02s so far)
   keep waiting: harnex result slow-bench
```

`harnex result NAME` blocks again (another 9 minutes by default) and prints the
result in the same format once it lands, even if the worker finished between
calls.

## Review and land

```bash
git diff HEAD...harnex/word-count     # read the change
(cd .harnex/worktrees/word-count && bin/test)
harnex land word-count
```

`harnex land NAME` merges `harnex/NAME` into the current branch of the main
checkout, then removes the worktree and the branch. Leftover uncommitted
changes in the lane are committed first. `harnex land` with no name lands every
finished worktree lane you started in this repo, oldest first.

**Conflicts.** When the merge conflicts, git's merge is left in progress and
harnex lists the files. Resolve them, `git add` them and `git commit`, then run
`harnex land NAME` again to clean up (or `git merge --abort` to give up).
Several lanes that touched the same file land one at a time.

**Merging by hand** works too. A lane whose branch is already in `HEAD` (and
whose worktree is clean) is tidied up by the next `delegate`, `result`, `lanes`
or bare `land`.

`harnex discard NAME` stops the lane if it is still working and deletes its
worktree and branch without merging.

**Lanes in place.** For a lane without a worktree, the footer counts only the
commits the worker made (harnex watches `HEAD` around each git command the
worker runs). Commits someone else made in the same checkout meanwhile are
named apart: `0 commits (HEAD also moved 3 commits by others)`.

## Parallel lanes

```bash
harnex delegate --no-wait --worktree slugify  "Fix TextKit.slugify so punctuation is dropped ..."
harnex delegate --no-wait --worktree truncate "Add TextKit.truncate(text, n) ..."
harnex delegate --no-wait --worktree titleize "Add TextKit.titleize(text) ..."
harnex result          # waits for all three, printing each result as it lands
harnex land            # lands every finished worktree lane, oldest first
```

`harnex result` with no names covers every lane you started in this repo whose
result you have not collected yet. Name lanes to wait for specific ones.
"You" is the calling agent session (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` or
`PI_SESSION_ID`); a Claude Code subagent shares its parent's id, so a subagent
should name the lanes it waits for.

## Follow-ups

```bash
harnex reply word-count "Also add TextKit.char_count(text), in the same style, with a test."
```

The worker keeps its context. A worker still on its turn takes the message
mid-task as a follow-up; a lane that has finished is relaunched on its own Pi
session (`pi --session`), so it remembers everything from the earlier turns.
The footer's cost is the lane's total so far.

**Messages from someone else.** Anyone can `harnex send` to a lane's worker
(the owner from another terminal, a buddy). The lane's result then says so,
so the session that started the lane is not left guessing:

```text
[earlier reply this turn, before another message reached the worker]
Review: PASS (0 P1, 2 P2) ...

[latest reply]
Understood; the report is now in /tmp/review.md.

── review: done in 6m10s · gpt-6.1-sol · $0.41 · 0 commits
   interjected: 1 message reached the worker from outside this lane (the reply above may answer it; all: `harnex events --id review`):
     23:26:04 from a terminal (harnex send): "Write the report to /tmp/review.md instead"
```

The worker's earlier answers in the same turn (the original task's report
among them) come first; your own `harnex reply` follow-ups are never listed as
interjections.

## When a model fails

```text
── word-count: FAILED after 3s (API error (404): model_not_found) · gpt-9 · $0.00 · 0 commits
   next: `harnex reply word-count "Continue the same task from where you stopped" --model openai/gpt-5.1`
         (keeps the task; another model) or `harnex discard word-count`
```

For provider and model failures (not found, rate limited, out of capacity) the
footer suggests continuing on Pi's default model. `reply --model` resumes the
same session, so the task is not lost. For `ask`, `--fallback-model` does this
automatically on `provider_capacity` only.

A provider refusal is different: `policy_refusal` means the provider refused
the content, so a retry needs a rephrased brief or another route. Do not send
"Continue the same task" unchanged. `provider_error_unexplained` means Pi
reported exactly `Unknown error (no error details in response)`; read the
provider/gateway logs before retrying. Harnex does not infer a policy refusal
when Pi supplies no details.

## Watching a worker

```bash
harnex lanes
```

```text
NAME      STATE                  AGE    MODEL    BRANCH           NEXT
slugify   working (now bash 12s) 1m40s  gpt-5.1  harnex/slugify   harnex result slugify
truncate  done                   2m03s  gpt-5.1  harnex/truncate  harnex land truncate
```

A working lane shows the tool it is running right now (tool names only; harnex
never records tool arguments). `harnex lanes --json` and MCP `lanes` return
current settlement (`done`/`failed` even before collection), a separate
`collected` boolean, and process-liveness `live`. `collected: false` means
`harnex result` still needs to collect the turn; listing does not do that.
The table keeps `finished, uncollected` for those finished workers.
`harnex pane --id NAME --lines 40` captures the
worker's tmux window, and the window itself is always there to watch.

## Where things live

- **Lane records:** `~/.local/state/harnex/lanes/` (one JSON file per lane:
  repo, worktree, branch, model, owner, Pi session, cost, last result). Closed
  lanes are pruned after 30 days; open lanes never are.
- **Worktrees:** `.harnex/worktrees/NAME` inside your repository, on branch
  `harnex/NAME`. To keep them beside the main checkout instead, set templates
  in the repo's `.harnex/config.json` (`{name}`, `{yyyy}`, `{mm}`, `{dd}`;
  the path is relative to the main checkout). `land` and `discard` follow the
  lane's own path and branch:

  ```json
  { "lanes": { "worktree_path": "../night-{mm}{dd}_{name}", "branch": "night/{mm}{dd}_{name}" } }
  ```

- **Bare-repo layouts** (`repo/.bare` plus sibling worktrees): the main
  checkout is the worktree on the bare repo's `HEAD` branch (`master`), and
  every worktree of the repo shares its lanes.
- **`.harnex/`** is added to the clone's `.git/info/exclude` the first time
  harnex writes there, so lane worktrees and dispatch rows never show up as
  untracked work. Nothing tracked changes.

## Habits from `harnex run`

The lane commands accept the flags people and agents reach for from the
low-level `run`, instead of refusing them: `--id NAME` and `--tmux NAME` name
the lane, `--auto-stop` and `--wait-done` are what lanes do anyway,
`--wait-timeout` means `--timeout`, and `--context`/`--context-file` give the
task.

See also: [MCP server](mcp.md), [Coding agents](agents.md), and the CLI
reference (`harnex help delegate`, `result`, `reply`, `land`, `discard`,
`lanes`, `ask`).


---

# MCP server

Source: https://harnex.zyt.app/docs/mcp

`harnex mcp` serves the [lane](lanes.md) commands as native
[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) tools over stdio.
Claude Code, Pi and any other MCP client can then hand work to Pi workers
without shelling out, quoting a brief, or looping on exit codes.

```bash
harnex mcp install     # register for Claude Code (user scope) and Pi
harnex mcp status      # where it is registered
harnex mcp uninstall   # remove both registrations
```

Restart running Claude Code and Pi sessions afterwards: clients load MCP
servers when a session starts. `harnex doctor` reports the registrations under
`integrations`.

## Tools

Each tool runs the matching CLI command and returns its text: normally the
worker's reply followed by the `── NAME:` footer. `lanes` returns the
`harnex lanes` table, with each worker's live activity; a settled worker reads
"finished, uncollected" until its result is collected. Scripts use
`harnex lanes --json`, whose `state` is `done`/`failed` for a settled worker
(never `running`), with separate `collected` and `live` fields.

| Tool | Arguments | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ask` | `question`; `model`, `effort`, `fallback_model`, `write`, `cwd`, `wait_minutes` | A read-only answer from a Pi worker |
| `delegate` | `task`; `worktree`, `name`, `wait`, `model`, `effort`, `cwd`, `wait_minutes` | A worker does the task (in a worktree when `worktree` is set) |
| `result` | `names`; `cwd`, `wait_minutes` | Wait for lanes and return each result |
| `reply` | `name`, `message`; `model`, `wait`, `cwd`, `wait_minutes` | Follow-up to the same worker, which keeps its context |
| `land` | `names` (optional); `cwd` | Merge worktree lanes, remove worktrees and branches |
| `discard` | `names`; `cwd` | Drop lanes without merging |
| `lanes` | `all`; `cwd` | Open lane JSON: settled state, collection, liveness, model and branch |

Arguments are forgiving: `prompt`, `brief` or `message` work for `task`;
`prompt` or `query` for `question`; `lane` or `id` for `name`. `cwd` defaults
to the server's working directory, which MCP clients set to the project.

## Long calls

A blocking call (`ask`, `delegate`, `reply`, `result`) waits up to
`wait_minutes` (default 25) and then returns "still working" with the lane name;
the worker keeps going and `result` collects it. While it waits, the server
sends `notifications/progress` every 15 seconds:

```text
word-count: working 2m10s · 7 tool calls · now bash 12s
```

Progress resets the clients' idle timers (Claude Code's 30-minute stdio idle
timeout, Pi's per-request timeout), and Claude Code shows it under the running
tool call.

- **Claude Code, main conversation:** a call still running after two minutes
  moves to a background task on its own; Claude keeps working and is notified
  when the result lands. A plain `delegate` therefore behaves like a background
  subagent.
- **Claude Code subagents and headless runs** block on the call. Headless
  `claude -p` stops background work ten idle minutes after the main turn ends;
  set `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0` for longer unattended runs.
- **Pi:** `harnex mcp install` registers the server with `exposure: direct`
  (the tools are declared to the model like built-ins) and a two-hour request
  timeout.
- **Cancelling** a call (for example pressing Esc) stops the wait, not the
  worker; `lanes` and `result` still see it.

Calls run concurrently, so a client can start several `delegate` calls with
`wait: false` and collect them with one `result`.

## Workers never get harnex's tools

Pi keeps MCP tools even when a worker is limited with `--tools`, so a worker
started by harnex would otherwise see `delegate` and could start more workers,
or escape a read-only ask. harnex prevents both: every Pi worker starts with
`--exclude-tools mcp__harnex__…`, and a read-only ask worker starts with
`--no-mcp`.

## Other clients

Any client that speaks MCP over stdio can run the server. The command is the
`harnex` executable with the argument `mcp`. Prefer the absolute path of the
RubyGems wrapper, `$(ruby -e 'print Gem.bindir')/harnex`, which is what
`harnex mcp install` registers, so no version-manager shim or working
directory gets in the way:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "harnex": { "command": "/path/to/bin/harnex", "args": ["mcp"] }
  }
}
```

The server negotiates MCP protocol revisions 2024-11-05 through 2025-11-25
and declares only the `tools` capability.

## Troubleshooting

- **The tools don't appear:** restart the client session; check
  `harnex mcp status` and, for Pi, `pi mcp list`.
- **A call ends with "still working":** that is the wait limit, not a failure;
  call `result` with the lane name.
- **A worker failed on its model:** the footer suggests
  `reply` with another `model`, which keeps the task.


---

# Coding agents

Source: https://harnex.zyt.app/docs/agents

harnex is built to be driven by coding agents: Claude Code, Pi, or anything
that can run a shell command or call an MCP tool. A supervising agent hands a
question or a task to a Pi worker (a GPT model by default), keeps working, and
gets the worker's reply back as plain text it can act on.

There are three ways in, from smoothest to most portable:

1. **MCP tools** (`harnex mcp install`): `ask`, `delegate`, `result`,
   `reply`, `land`, `discard` and `lanes` as native tools. See
   [MCP server](mcp.md).
2. **The `gpt` subagent** for Claude Code: a background subagent that relays
   one brief to a worker and returns the reply verbatim.
3. **The CLI** from any agent's shell tool: the same verbs as
   [lanes](lanes.md).

## Claude Code

### MCP tools (main conversation)

With the server registered, Claude calls the tools directly. A call that runs
longer than two minutes moves to the background on its own; Claude keeps
working and is notified when the result lands, so a `delegate` behaves like a
background subagent without one:

```text
❯ Use the harnex delegate tool to have a GPT worker run the slow benchmark and tell me the score.
● Calling harnex…
  ⎿  pi-slow-bench: working 59s · 3 tool calls · now bash 44s
● The GPT worker is still running the benchmark. I'll report the score when it finishes.
● MCP task (harnex/delegate) completed.
● The score is 302926.
```

### The `gpt` subagent

`harnex mcp install` also installs a `gpt` agent definition at
`~/.claude/agents/gpt.md` when none exists. It is a thin Haiku relay with only
the harnex tools: it never does the task itself and returns the worker's reply
exactly, footer included. Use it for parallel work (several `Agent` calls in
one message) and for follow-ups (`SendMessage` to the same agent reaches the
same worker, with its context).

```text
Agent(subagent_type: "gpt", prompt: """
worktree: word-count

Add TextKit.word_count(text) to lib/textkit.rb with a test; run bin/test.
""")
```

Optional header lines, then a blank line, then the brief:

| Header | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `worktree: NAME` | Edit in a new worktree on `harnex/NAME`; land it afterwards |
| `mode: write` | Run commands or edit the current checkout in place |
| `mode: read` | Read-only, even if the brief mentions commands |
| `model: provider/model`, `effort: low\|medium\|high` | Pick the worker's model |
| `fallback: provider/model` | Retry a read-only ask on another model |
| `cwd: DIR` | Work in another directory, e.g. a sibling worktree (follow-ups stay there) |
| `name: NAME` | Name the lane (default: the `cwd` worktree's name, else the brief's first words) |

Without a header, questions and reviews go to a read-only worker, and a brief
that asks to run something or change files goes to a worker that can. Only
header lines set these: a brief that mentions a worktree or a branch is passed
on as it is, never turned into a `worktree`.
The definition ships with harnex as [`agents/gpt.md`](../agents/gpt.md).

### The CLI from Claude's Bash tool

```bash
harnex delegate --worktree word-count "Add TextKit.word_count(text) with a test; run bin/test."
```

Give the Bash call `timeout: 600000`: commands wait up to 9 minutes, and
Claude Code's default Bash timeout is two minutes. On exit 124 run
`harnex result NAME`. In the main conversation, `run_in_background` works too.

### Things worth knowing

- Claude Code loads agent definitions and MCP servers when a session starts;
  restart after `harnex mcp install`.
- Background results reach the parent XML-escaped (`&amp;`, `&lt;`). The relay's
  own text is exact.
- Headless `claude -p` stops background work ten idle minutes after the main
  turn; set `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0` for long unattended runs.

## Pi

`harnex mcp install` adds the server to `~/.pi/agent/mcp.json` with
`exposure: direct`, so a Pi supervisor sees the tools like built-ins. Without
MCP, Pi uses the CLI through its `bash` tool; `harnex agents-guide claude` is
the short guide it needs (it applies to any supervising agent). Workers
started by harnex never see harnex's own MCP tools, so a worker cannot start
more workers.

## Habits that keep it smooth

- **Self-contained briefs.** The worker has not seen your conversation: name
  the files, the expected behavior and the check (`bin/test`).
- **A worktree for anything that edits.** `--worktree NAME` keeps parallel
  lanes apart and your checkout clean until you land.
- **Verify, then land.** `done` means the worker's turn ended without error,
  not that the work is right. Read the diff and run the tests yourself.
- **Land, don't merge by hand.** `land` also removes the worktree and branch.
- **Check on a worker with `lanes`.** It shows the tool each worker is running
  now.

## Measuring it

`evals/agents/run` drives real supervisors (Claude Code headless and Pi print
mode, each with and without MCP) through seven scenarios against a fixture
repository and scores correctness, tool calls, harnex usage errors, doc
lookups and leftovers. harnex 0.29 passes all 28 runs with no harnex usage
errors, no doc lookups and nothing left behind.

```bash
evals/agents/run --list
evals/agents/run --supervisor claude,pi S2 S3
```


---

# Upgrading to 0.29

Source: https://harnex.zyt.app/docs/upgrading

harnex 0.29 is the agent release. It adds lanes (`delegate`, `result`,
`reply`, `land`, `discard`, `lanes`), the `harnex mcp` server and the `gpt`
subagent for Claude Code. The low-level session commands (`run`, `send`, `wait`,
`watch`, `stop`, `status`, `pane`, `logs`, `events`) keep working as before.

The last RubyGems release before this one was 0.12.0. If you are upgrading
from it, read the whole page; from 0.21 on, only the 0.22 section applies.

```bash
gem install harnex          # 0.29.0
harnex --version
harnex doctor               # checks Pi; reports MCP and agent integrations
harnex mcp install          # optional: native tools for Claude Code and Pi
pi update                   # harnex needs Pi 0.80.4+; MCP features want 1.0.4+
```

## Breaking changes

### Codex support was removed (0.20)

harnex now runs Pi workers backed by GPT and other models; Pi's structured RPC
mode is the worker path that is designed, tested and supported. Removed:

- the `codex` and `codex app-server` adapters and the JSON-RPC session
  transport;
- `harnex run --fast` and `--legacy-pty`, and `harnex preflight --legacy-pty`;
- the Codex checks in `harnex doctor` (it checks Pi; `--adapter pi|all`).

`harnex run codex` is no longer special-cased; it wraps a `codex` binary as a
generic PTY program. Claude Code, OpenCode and any other terminal CLI still run
under a PTY as before. Dispatch rows keep their schema; Codex-only fields stay
`null` in new rows.

### `harnex ask` waits 9 minutes by default (0.22)

`ask` used to wait without a limit. It now stops waiting after 9 minutes (the
worker keeps going) and exits 124, naming `harnex result ID`, which keeps
waiting and prints the answer. Pass `--timeout none` for the old behavior.
`ask --resume ID` still works and no longer needs `--repo`.

### Pi starts with `--no-approve` (0.22)

Pi's RPC mode cannot show its project-trust prompt, so harnex now starts every
Pi worker with `--no-approve`: project-local Pi resources (`.pi/` extensions,
skills, prompts) are ignored unless you pass `-- --approve`. Before, the result
depended on Pi's default.

### Workers never see harnex's own MCP tools (0.25)

When harnex is registered as an MCP server in Pi, every Pi worker harnex
starts gets `--exclude-tools mcp__harnex__…`, and a read-only ask worker gets
`--no-mcp`. A worker can no longer start other workers. Your own `--tools`
and `--exclude-tools` still apply (the exclusions are merged).

## What's new, briefly

- **Lanes** — `delegate` hands a task to a worker (optionally in its own git
  worktree) and prints its reply with a footer of state, model, cost, commits
  and next steps. `result` collects parallel lanes, `reply` follows up with the
  worker's context (a finished lane resumes its Pi session), `land` merges and
  cleans up, `discard` drops a lane, `lanes` shows what each worker is doing.
  See [Lanes](lanes.md).
- **`harnex mcp`** — the same verbs as native MCP tools for Claude Code, Pi and
  any MCP client, with progress notifications for long calls. See
  [MCP server](mcp.md).
- **The `gpt` subagent** for Claude Code, installed by `harnex mcp install`.
  See [Coding agents](agents.md).
- **Hygiene** — harnex adds `.harnex/` to the clone's `.git/info/exclude`, so
  lane worktrees and dispatch rows never show up as untracked work.
- **`harnex doctor`** reports `integrations` (MCP registrations, the agent)
  and new capabilities (`lanes`, `mcp`, `ask_resume`).
- **`wait --since TIME`** ignores events from an earlier launch of a reused
  session id.

## If something looks different

| You see | Why | Do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ask` exits 124 after 9 minutes | new default wait | `harnex result ID`, or `--timeout none` |
| A Pi worker ignores `.pi/` resources | `--no-approve` by default | `harnex run pi ... -- --approve` |
| `harnex run codex` behaves like a plain PTY program | Codex adapters removed | use Pi workers (`harnex delegate`, `harnex run pi`) |
| A new `.harnex/` line in `.git/info/exclude` | harnex hides its own state | nothing; it is local to the clone |
| Workers lack `mcp__harnex__*` tools | recursion guard | intended |

The full history is in the [changelog](../CHANGELOG.md).
